Package neqsim.process.equipment.compressor

Class RecycleFlowCoordinator

java.lang.Object
neqsim.util.NamedBaseClass
neqsim.process.SimulationBaseClass
neqsim.process.equipment.ProcessEquipmentBaseClass
neqsim.process.equipment.compressor.RecycleFlowCoordinator
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, Runnable, ProcessEquipmentInterface, ProcessElementInterface, SimulationInterface, NamedInterface
public class RecycleFlowCoordinator extends ProcessEquipmentBaseClass
Reconciles a valve-calculated anti-surge recycle flow with a compressor discharge split.

Dynamic process systems execute equipment sequentially, so the recycle valve can calculate a requested flow after its discharge splitter has already run. This coordinator writes the accepted, bounded flow back to both branches and updates the splitter specification for the next step. The current accepted state is therefore mass conserving while retaining the ordered transient dependency break provided by Recycle.

    • runTransient

      public void runTransient(double dt, UUID id)
      runTransient This method calculates thermodynamic and unit operations using difference equations if available and calculateSteadyState is true. Use setCalculateSteadyState to set the parameter. Sets calc identifier UUID.

      Steady-state equipment may be evaluated repeatedly with the same calculation identifier while a transient solver refines one physical timestep. Every evaluation still calls SimulationInterface.run(UUID), but the equipment clock advances only for the first successful evaluation of a non-null identifier. For a null identifier, every successful evaluation advances the clock. The default transient boundary does not set an identifier in that case, so any identifier mutation performed by run(null) is retained.

      Parameters:
      dt - Delta time [s]
      id - Calculation identifier
